system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (buyer side)
**Scope note:** The Seller's framing ("fair and balanced", "settled", "adequate", "addressed") is advocacy, not fact. Reviewed strictly against the Buyer Playbook. No Amelia Frost written authority for any fallback position has been given, so no fallback is available on this draft.

---

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer wants | Recommendation & reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** | General liability cap | Cl 12.1: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 starting position | **REJECT – counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** 20% is only our conditional fallback and requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft; none exists, so it cannot be conceded. |
| **SPA-N-002** | De minimis & basket | Cl 12.2: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery | De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery | **REJECT all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x ours on each number and the deductible structure permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 – compounded with the cap this guts practical recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003** | General claims time limit | Cl 12.3/13: 18 months; plus "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | 24 months after Completion; limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims | **REJECT – counter at 24 months and delete the catch-all.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (not given), and the "applies to all Claims" language is a hidden override of every separate regime (see N-014). |
| **SPA-N-004** | Fundamental/Title regime | Capacity and title warranties subject to same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% of price cap, at least 6 years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | **REJECT outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap a AUD 24m title failure at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month window; this is a market-standard separate regime and non-negotiable. |
| **SPA-N-005** | Fraud carve-out | Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5: limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" – no fraud carve-out anywhere | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable | **REJECT – insert express carve-out.** The draft purports to cap and time-bar fraud, which is unacceptable and likely unenforceable; no one on our side has authority to waive this. |
| **SPA-N-006** | Disclosure scope | Sch 7 / DL [1.1]–[1.2]: whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 Sept 2026, Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" deemed disclosed; [1.4] denies all admissions | Specific, fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | **REJECT general disclosures [1.1]–[1.2].** Blanket deemed disclosure shifts the entire diligence risk to the Buyer and, combined with N-007, would make most warranties worthless. Require a "fair disclosure, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope" standard, specific disclosures only. |
| **SPA-N-007** | Buyer knowledge qualifier | Cl 8.3: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, with Seller warranties qualified by named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | **REJECT and delete cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that duplicates the deemed-disclosure problem and would bar nearly every claim; at most accept actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team members, expressly excluding title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities. |
| **SPA-N-008** | Bluefen consent (~30% revenue, ~AUD 3.6m) | Cl 3/6.3: "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. DL [2] confirms **no final written consent and no evidence of cl 11.3 conditions** in the data room | Condition precedent: effective consent AND evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; all-reasonable/best endeavours obligation | **REJECT – the matter is not "addressed", it is open.** For a customer representing ~30% of revenue, consent-on-delivery without proof the 11.3 conditions are met leaves the Buyer exposed to a conditional or ineffective consent; make it a hard CP with Buyer satisfaction on the conditions evidence. |
| **SPA-N-009** | Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m) | Cl 2/7: release "to be provided following Completion". DL [3]: not repaid; no final discharge of security included | Current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases delivered at Completion. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval | **REJECT post-completion release.** A debt-free/cash-free deal cannot complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and undischarged security over the target; require Completion-day payout letter, direct payment in the funds flow and executed releases/PPSR discharges. Post-completion is only possible with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost sign-off, neither of which exists. |
| **SPA-N-010** | Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000) | Funds flow silently excludes them – "a matter for the Seller". DL [5]: conditional on Completion and continued employment; silent on payroll tax, super, on-costs | AUD 420,000 **plus** triggered on-costs as a specific line item in the funds flow, or Seller-funded with a price adjustment/indemnity | **REJECT the silent exclusion.** These are Completion-triggered liabilities that will sit in the Company post-Completion; if not itemised or Seller-funded, the Buyer is paying them a second time. Require quantification of super/payroll tax on-costs and a specific line item or indemnity. |
| **SPA-N-011** | Ironquay IP indemnity | Cl 11.1: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate". DL [4]: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all fees; AUD 180,000 shown open in DD-010 but not bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room | Broadened indemnity covering ownership/title to and use of SOW3 Project Materials, infringement claims and loss from non-transfer; preserve the SOW3 payment cure (pay and obtain assignment pre-Completion) | **REJECT "adequate" – broaden the indemnity.** The risk is that IP in deliverables has not transferred at all, not merely an AUD 180,000 payment; require pre-Completion payment and confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, with a specific indemnity outside the general regime. Treat AUD 180,000 as unverified in either direction. |
| **SPA-N-012** | Export/privacy incident (DD-006, ~1,240 records) | Cl 4.6/Sch 6: "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". DL [6]: access, scope and notification duty all unestablished; investigation preliminary; no loss stated | Log preservation, completed investigation, periodic updates to Completion, specific indemnity for notification/regulatory/third-party costs if a breach is later established; no assumption of breach or harm either way | **DO NOT ACCEPT "not material" – it is unassessed, not immaterial.** Require a covenant to preserve logs, complete the investigation, update the Buyer before Completion, and a specific indemnity for any resulting costs; no numeric demand or price adjustment is justified on current facts. |
| **SPA-N-013** | Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) | "Ordinary-course operating costs". DL [8]: three x AUD 110,000; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course | Assess DD-008/DD-011 together; determine whether any amount is accrued/pre-Completion-referable (Working Capital or Debt) vs genuine forward operating cost | **ASSESS – do not accept or reject yet.** No automatic Debt classification or price deduction per playbook, but the Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by the disclosure; request renewal terms and accrual treatment before Completion Accounts mechanics are fixed. |
| **SPA-N-014** | Category separation | Cl 12.3/13 catch-all plus cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 collapse Title, Tax, IP, payment covenants and indemnities into the general regime | Title/Tax/IP/payment obligations/covenants/specific indemnities each kept separate with their own caps and periods; express statement that general limitations do not apply to them | **REJECT – delete the "applies to all Claims" override and insert express exclusions.** This single sentence is the mechanism by which N-004, N-005, N-011 and N-016 are silently defeated; it is the most important drafting point in the Seller's package. |
| **SPA-N-015** | Title verification | "Evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012". DL [10] concedes this is the source relied on and that no Buyer verification is assumed | Independent evidence: ASIC company extract, PPSR search, review of constitution/shareholder agreements, board minutes, share certificates, officer's and director's certificates, and seller authority (constitutional/board approval) | **REJECT register as sole evidence.** DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal document, not independent proof; title to 100% of the shares is the entire consideration and must be independently verified pre-Completion with a Completion-day title/encumbrance/authority deliverables list. |
| **SPA-N-016** | Tax / IP terms | "Settled under the general regime above" | Tax and IP remain OPEN; separate regimes to be negotiated (standard: Tax – separate indemnity, period tied to statutory review periods; IP – separate cap/period); no unlimited liability assumed | **REJECT the "settled" characterisation – record as OPEN.** Nothing has been agreed; the Seller is attempting to bind these categories to the 20%/18-month general regime by assertion. Respond in writing that Tax and IP remain under negotiation and no agreement is implied. |

---

## Overarching observations

1. **Structural design, not isolated points.** The Seller's draft combines (a) a low cap, (b) high deductible thresholds, (c) a short period, (d) a catch-all sweeping every category into those limits, (e) whole-data-room disclosure and (f) a "discoverable" knowledge bar. Each alone is aggressive; together they would leave the Buyer with little or no effective warranty protection on a AUD 24m acquisition. The response should reject the package as a whole and reset to playbook, not trade individual items.

2. **The Disclosure Letter contradicts the Update.** The Seller Update describes Bluefen, Riverlark and Ironquay as "addressed"/"adequate", while the Disclosure Letter (paras 2–4) confirms that none of the underlying deliverables exist in the data room. We should cite the Seller's own disclosures back to them.

3. **No fallback is live.** Both fallbacks the Seller has landed on (20% cap, 18 months) require Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. None has been given; the deal team should not signal flexibility on either until that authority is obtained, if at all.

4. **Completion deliverables to add.** Bluefen effective consent + 11.3 evidence; Riverlark payout letter + releases; Ironquay payment receipt + confirmatory assignment; DD-005 on-cost quantification; independent title pack; DD-006 investigation update.

5. **Items to leave open, not concede.** Sandbar (assess), DD-006 (no breach or no-breach assumed), Ironquay AUD 180,000 (unverified), Tax/IP (open).

Happy to convert this into a formal mark-up of the SPA clauses or an issues-list response to Harbourglass's counsel if useful.
=== END ADVICE ===
